findings.claim: Arteries are defined as vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart.
findings.truth: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. They usually carry oxygenated blood, but the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
findings.evidence: Great Ormond Street Hospital, ‘Transposition of the great arteries’ (fetched): the pulmonary artery takes blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen; spec 1.1.1 names the pulmonary artery.

findings.claim: The cardiovascular system is described as ‘the systemic or pulmonary circulatory system’.
findings.truth: For this specification, the cardiovascular system is the systemic circulatory system; the cardio-respiratory system is the pulmonary circulatory system.

findings.claim: The lesson says the skeletal system has six functions and that all six may be tested individually.
findings.truth: The assessable muscular-skeletal content names movement types, antagonistic action, muscle attachment, protection, and the body’s structure and shape. It does not name red-blood-cell production or mineral storage. Either replace the cross-field ‘six functions’ teaching and questions with the specified content, or retain it explicitly as unassessed enrichment.
findings.evidence: spec pp. 9–11: the amplification is the full assessable content unless qualified; spec 1.1.2

findings.claim: At rest, blood is shared fairly evenly across all the organs.
findings.truth: At rest, blood flow is distributed according to organs’ different needs; it is not shared evenly.
findings.evidence: NCBI Bookshelf, ‘The Oxygen Cascade During Exercise in Health and Disease’ (fetched): most resting cardiac output goes to the brain, heart and visceral organs.

findings.claim: Anaerobic exercise is said to produce ‘lactic acid’, which causes burning and is cleared through EPOC; the same account appears in questions, checks and flashcards.
findings.truth: The physiological product is lactate, and fatigue and EPOC have several causes; most lactate is oxidised rather than converted to glucose. Revise every linked field to a single age-appropriate lactate explanation, or retain the current school shorthand only after the content owner confirms it is intentional.
findings.evidence: PMC, ‘Lactate as a fulcrum of metabolism’ and ‘Combustion, Respiration and Intermittent Exercise’ (fetched)

findings.claim: Long-term adaptations are called permanent changes.
findings.truth: Training adaptations are long-lasting but can reverse partly or fully when training stops.
findings.evidence: PubMed, ‘Cardiorespiratory and metabolic consequences of detraining in endurance athletes’ (fetched): training adaptations can be partially or entirely reversed after habitual activity stops.

findings.claim: A larger stroke volume ‘clears excess oxygen debt’ more efficiently.
findings.truth: EPOC is elevated oxygen use while the body recovers; it is not an oxygen debt cleared by stroke volume alone.
findings.evidence: PMC, ‘Combustion, Respiration and Intermittent Exercise’ (fetched): EPOC replaced the oxygen-debt model and has multiple recovery mechanisms.

findings.claim: Regular aerobic training is said to increase vital capacity and create denser capillary networks around alveoli, and these are presented as the two main respiratory adaptations.
findings.truth: The specification requires changes to respiratory values and capillarisation but does not name vital capacity or an alveolar location. Research finds no or only minor lung-function changes after weeks or months of endurance training in healthy people, while evidence on pulmonary capillary change is mixed. Either use the specification’s neutral terms throughout, or retain the detailed claims only with curriculum-owner confirmation.
findings.evidence: spec 1.1.4; PMC, ‘Is the Lung Built for Exercise?’ and ‘Effect of aerobic fitness on capillary blood volume and diffusing membrane capacity responses to exercise’ (fetched)

findings.claim: The lesson repeatedly says anaerobic exercise produces lactic acid, that lactic acid dissociates into lactate and hydrogen ions, and that lactate clearance is mainly conversion to glucose in the liver.
findings.truth: At physiological pH, the relevant metabolite is lactate; fatigue and lactate use are more complex, and much lactate is oxidised. A correction would change the collapsible, questions, checks and flashcards, so choose a unit-wide, age-appropriate lactate explanation before editing.
findings.evidence: PMC, ‘Lactate as a fulcrum of metabolism’ and ‘Hyperlactatemia and Cardiac Surgery’ (fetched)

summary: Four lessons were checked. Five verified issues have surgical edits; four wider scope or physiology issues are held for adjudication.
